description: Resume a stale-settings fix after Session A tried and rejected mtime-only invalidation under same-metadata rewrites.

repository_visible: The current cache stores parsed settings forever by path.
Session A added a regression that rewrites the same path with the same size and forced timestamp.
The attempted mtime implementation was reverted, so it is absent from the checkpoint diff.
semantic_handoff: The former decision to use mtime-only invalidation is deprecated.
The rejection reason is that overlay and network filesystems can preserve coarse timestamps, including for same-size rewrites.
The replacement decision prioritizes fresh reads and permits content identity or removal of this micro-cache, but not stat metadata alone.
The public load_settings(path) signature must stay stable.
construction_facts.fairness_note: The summary and transcript explicitly carry both the deprecated direction and its status/reason. The Intent condition must render decision status and deprecation reason rather than merely listing both directions.

session_a.goal: Investigate why an mtime-based stale-settings fix still fails on some deployment filesystems.
session_a.checkpoint_goal: Add a helper that writes JSON while restoring a fixed mtime and a failing regression named test_reload_observes_same_metadata_rewrite. The rewritten JSON must have the same byte length. Revert any production experiment and stop with settings/cache.py unchanged.
session_a.chat_summary: Session A proved that the proposed mtime-only cache invalidation is not correct on filesystems that preserve or coarsen timestamps. It added a same-path, same-size, fixed-mtime regression and reverted the experiment, leaving production code unchanged. The old mtime-only decision is deprecated. The active replacement prioritizes fresh content and permits content identity or removing this micro-cache, while preserving load_settings(path) and adding no watcher dependency.
session_a.transcript: User: The mtime invalidation fix still serves old settings in a container volume. Agent: I reproduced it by writing two same-length JSON documents to the same path and restoring an identical nanosecond timestamp. The mtime-only implementation cannot distinguish them. User: Keep the failed attempt? Agent: I reverted the production experiment so the checkpoint contains only the deterministic regression. I marked the mtime-only direction deprecated with the filesystem reason. The replacement decision favors correctness: content identity or no micro-cache are acceptable, stat metadata alone is not. load_settings(path) remains stable and we should not add a watcher dependency.

changes.tests/fake_fs.py:
import json
import os


def write_json(path, value):
    path.write_text(json.dumps(value), encoding="utf-8")


def write_json_with_fixed_mtime(path, value, stamp_ns):
    write_json(path, value)
    os.utime(path, ns=(stamp_ns, stamp_ns))

from settings.app import greeting
from settings.cache import load_settings
from tests.fake_fs import write_json, write_json_with_fixed_mtime


def test_load_settings_reads_json(tmp_path):
    path = tmp_path / "settings.json"
    write_json(path, {"name": "Ada"})
    assert load_settings(path) == {"name": "Ada"}
    assert greeting(path) == "hello Ada"


def test_reload_observes_same_metadata_rewrite(tmp_path):
    path = tmp_path / "settings.json"
    stamp_ns = 1_700_000_000_000_000_000
    write_json_with_fixed_mtime(path, {"name": "Ada"}, stamp_ns)
    assert greeting(path) == "hello Ada"

    write_json_with_fixed_mtime(path, {"name": "Eve"}, stamp_ns)
    assert greeting(path) == "hello Eve"

intent.what: Make settings reloads observe content changes reliably
intent.why: Long-running processes must not serve stale configuration after an operator replaces a file in place.

snaps.what: Reproduced a same-path, same-size rewrite with an unchanged mtime and reverted the failed production experiment
snaps.why: The checkpoint preserves the evidence while ensuring Git alone does not present the rejected implementation as current work.

decisions.what: Use file mtime as the cache invalidation identity
decisions.why: It originally appeared to provide cheap invalidation without rereading content.
decisions.reason: Overlay and network filesystems can retain or coarsen timestamps, so same-size rewrites can remain invisible.

decisions.what: Prioritize fresh content over the settings micro-cache and never rely on stat metadata alone
decisions.why: Configuration correctness matters more than avoiding a small local file read; content identity or removing the cache are both acceptable.

must_contain.reason: Session A should leave the same-metadata regression.
The reproduction must pin the timestamp after each write.

must_equal.reason: The rejected production attempt must be absent at the canonical checkpoint.

must_contain.reason: The established loader signature must remain available.

must_equal.reason: The correction does not require a file watcher or third-party dependency.
